articles.title: Dollar jumps after strong US payrolls report
articles.desc: The US dollar index jumped significantly following the Labor Department's report indicating an increase of 165,000 jobs last month, which far exceeded economists' forecasts. As a result, the probability of a rate hike from the Federal Reserve climbed to nearly 80% for next month. Moreover, Federal Reserve officials voiced concerns about ongoing inflation, leading to declines for other currencies such as the euro and sterling against the dollar.

articles.title: Gold drops as strong US payrolls boost dollar, yields
articles.desc: In light of stronger-than-anticipated US payroll figures, gold prices dipped significantly as the data suggested a robust labor market. This development heightened expectations for sustained high-interest rates from the Federal Reserve, bolstering the dollar's strength. Spot gold saw a decline of 0.3% to reach $4,074.36 per ounce, while US gold futures fell by 0.9%. However, Indian retail demand picked up ahead of Diwali festivities, taking advantage of the lower prices.

articles.title: Risk-off mood sweeps European stocks as AI concerns deepen
articles.desc: European markets saw a 1% dip as a wave of selloffs hit insurance stocks following a Democratic victory, raising concerns around the stability of AI investments. A significant downgrade of German reinsurers by JPMorgan added to the insurance sector's woes. Yet, clean energy stocks thrived, bolstered by renewed support for green initiatives.

articles.title: Wall Street stocks rally after heavy AI-related selloff
articles.desc: Wall Street's trading session presented a mixed scenario as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq climbed, contrasting with a modest dip in the Dow. Investor apprehensions regarding impending regulations for the AI sector, especially after recent Democratic electoral successes, led to increased market volatility. Meanwhile, key global markets witnessed declines, particularly in Europe and Asia, overshadowing advancements in certain tech stocks amid a generally bearish sentiment.

articles.title: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
articles.desc: On Friday, technology stocks saw a significant rebound, boosting investor optimism about growth in artificial intelligence amidst recent market fluctuations. The semiconductor sector soared, primarily driven by impressive gains from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices. Although this recovery was strong, the Nasdaq recorded its fourth consecutive weekly fall, hinting at a mixed market outlook. Job indicators remain strong, influencing Federal Reserve interest rate hike expectations.

articles.desc: On Friday, the government launched the web application portal for Semicon 2.0, which will initially receive applications related to three of the programme's six pillars: machines and materials, fabs, and packaging. Guidelines have so far been issued only for these three pillars, and the portal is now inviting applications for them. Other three areas pertain to design, R&D and talent.

Increased allocation under the SASCI scheme is expected to support infrastructure spending, particularly urban development, roads and bridges.

articles.desc: This week, Indian government bonds saw a remarkable performance, outpacing other Asian markets as benchmark yields dropped significantly. Following the Democratic win in the US midterms, crude prices fell sharply, enticing foreign investors back to purchase a significant volume of Indian bonds. This shift alleviates pressure on the Reserve Bank of India to maintain elevated yields, contributing to a positive outlook for Indian debt moving forward.

articles.title: British Airways parent profit drops on higher fuel costs
articles.desc: IAG, the owner of British Airways and Iberia, said Friday that its net profit dropped more than 12 percent in the third quarter on soaring fuel costs and flight disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict. The group said its overall flight capacity had been hit "by cancellations due to the conflict in the Middle East, together with aircraft availability linked to engine issues and disruption related to air traffic control disruption".

articles.title: Trump Media's investors lost $2.2 billion while Trump holds $460 million stake

Many investors had high hopes for the social media platform, believing in its potential profitability under Trump's leadership. Instead, Trump Media's shares have lost significant value, and discontent among shareholders has grown. The company's revenue remains stagnant, leading investors to question management practices and investor trust.

articles.title: Copper price falls for 4th day, heads for worst week since March on AI rout
articles.desc: Copper prices have faced yet another decline, marking four consecutive sessions of decrease, primarily due to a dip in technology shares and rising concerns over artificial intelligence investments. The three-month copper rate on the London Metal Exchange fell to a low not seen since late July. While tight supply, particularly outside the US, has cushioned further losses, a significant drop in copper stocks within Chinese warehouses is intensifying supply anxieties.

articles.title: Siemens Q2 Results: Profit grows 5% to Rs 504 crore
articles.desc: Siemens Limited announced a consolidated net profit of Rs 504 crore for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. This represents a 4.78% increase compared to the previous year's profit of Rs 481 crore. Revenue from operations grew significantly to Rs 5,734 crore, up from Rs 4,900 crore a year prior. Additionally, new orders reached Rs 6,228 crore, a notable 38% increase year-over-year.

articles.title: Indian rupee strengthens past 94/$ as oil slides, foreign inflows return
articles.desc: The Indian rupee strengthened past 94 per dollar after regaining appeal among emerging-market currencies recently. Significant foreign inflows into Indian equities and a sharp fall in oil prices are key factors. Analysts suggest India's equity markets may attract global investments as concerns about AI infrastructure spending grow. The Reserve Bank of India announced measures to support the rupee against maintaining fluctuations.

articles.title: DGTR recommends imposition of quantitative restrictions on soda ash imports for 2 years
articles.desc: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies has signaled its intention to introduce protective measures to curb the influx of soda ash imports. This action responds to an appeal from the Alkali Manufacturers Association of India due to a troubling spike in imports. The proposed two-year quantitative restrictions will allocate specific quotas per country, distributing these annual restrictions in quarterly segments to ensure domestic manufacturers are protected.

articles.title: BMW Industries Q2 Results: Net profit rise 43% YoY to Rs 21.62 crore
articles.desc: BMW Industries Ltd has reported an impressive 42.7 percent increase in net profit for the quarter ending on September 30. The firm's total income surged by 33 percent compared to the same quarter last fiscal year, while EBITDA rose by 25 percent, showcasing its resilience and growth. Notably, the new greenfield downstream steel complex in Bokaro commenced operations, with future plans focused on optimizing capacity utilization across these facilities.

articles.title: HCC Q2 profit slumps 53% to Rs 22 crore
articles.desc: Hindustan Construction Company reported a decline in consolidated net profit for the September quarter of FY27. Income and expenses also saw a reduction in comparison to the previous year's figures. The company secured an order of Rs 524 crore and participated in several project bids. Additionally, construction progressed on various projects including the Indore and Patna Metro.

articles.title: India's October consumer inflation likely nears top of RBI target on food costs: Reuters poll
articles.desc: India's consumer inflation is projected to rise in October, mainly driven by significant increases in food prices. Economists expect food inflation to reach 8.20%, reflecting ongoing market pressures. Rising global food prices and higher input costs contribute to the inflationary environment. The Reserve Bank of India anticipates inflation to average 5.2% for the current financial year. A rate hike is likely to occur in the central bank's upcoming policy meeting.

articles.title: Rupee falls 9 paise to 94.50 against US dollar in early trade
articles.desc: In early trading on Friday, the rupee slipped by 9 paise to reach 94.50 against the US dollar, driven by a robust dollar and surging crude oil prices. After a brief bounce-back, it peaked at 94.36. The domestic equity market exhibited mixed performance, with Sensex rising yet Nifty falling. Notably, Foreign Institutional Investors remained active, purchasing substantial equities, bolstering market optimism.

articles.title: India bonds emerge as top Asian performers as oil, Treasury yields decline
articles.desc: This week, Indian government bonds saw a positive trend following a Democratic win in the U.S. midterm elections. The reduction in oil prices and Treasury yields eased rupee pressure, boosting investor confidence. The benchmark bond yield improved significantly, declining by approximately 22 basis points. Furthermore, the surge in foreign investments into Indian bonds marked a notable high since July, leading to enhanced overall market sentiment.

articles.title: India’s new wealth rituals: What are millennials and Gen Z buying on Dhanteras?
articles.desc: Dhanteras investing is evolving from physical gold purchases toward diversified digital portfolios. Younger investors are embracing gold ETFs, mutual funds, Bitcoin and tokenised assets while retaining the festival’s core goal of building wealth and financial security patiently.

articles.title: Beyond gold: What $340 billion in crypto flows says about India's investment preferences this Dhanteras
articles.desc: Gold remains central to Indian household savings, but high prices are pushing investors toward ETFs and digital gold instead of physical holdings. Crypto is emerging as a separate portfolio option rather than replacing gold, reflecting a broader shift toward digital ownership and diversification.

articles.title: Micron stock tanks 17% as AI chip selloff deepens: What's next?
articles.desc: Micron shares plunged 17% amid a broader semiconductor selloff driven by concerns over AI infrastructure spending and future chip demand. A reported pause in Taiwan facility construction added to investor worries, while technical indicators pointed to oversold conditions.

articles.title: Largecap dhamaka! 6 bluechip stocks with upside of up to 48% to buy this Diwali
articles.desc: As Samvat 2083 approaches, careful stock selection is vital due to global uncertainties. Religare Broking identifies six largecap stocks, such as Bajaj Finance and Mahindra Mahindra, that show promising upside this Diwali. With each stock displaying unique growth characteristics supporting their projected price targets, analysts stress the importance of sustainable earnings growth. A diversified portfolio is essential for effectively navigating the changing market dynamics.
